title: Released Cedar Creek data gave higher mean diversity variation under drought in 16-species plots in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether lower temporal diversity variation under drought repeats across planting groups and periods in a Cedar Creek experiment. The released data contain nine whole plots per planting group, four factorial subplots per plot and six years. In 16-species plots, mean six-year inverse Simpson CV was 0.2766 with ambient water and 0.3293 with drought. This positive descriptive contrast differs from the lower variation described in the source paper. Both heat strata gave a positive contrast. Four primary planting-group and period tests gave differences of -0.0569, -0.0186, +0.0527 and +0.0279. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Raw and log standard deviations kept the full-period directions but remained uncertain. A variance split showed lower shared annual variation and higher residual variation in 16-species plots under drought. This identity does not identify a biological mechanism. Small moving harvest strips, only three years per primary period, shared weather and one site limit inference. We do not establish a general drought effect or a proven cause of the source discrepancy. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, retrieval instructions and numerical checks are included. Raw data remain external.

display.caption: Drought-minus-ambient contrasts in inverse Simpson CV and log standard deviation. Intervals use a t8 cutoff with alpha 0.05/4. Four early and late CV contrasts form the primary family. Full-period and log SD results are diagnostics.
